WoW: Forever

Feral — Bear Druid

Leather tanking in Bear Form on rage, armour and dodge: no block, no parry. This is your only combat form between levels 10 and 20, so every Druid plays it whether they intend to tank or not.

Back to top

A guide to the live game, 1 to 60. Numbers are the client's at build 1.60.1.70938 with Blizzard's hotfixes through November 12. Talent orders are Icy Veins' and Wowhead's published builds, named and dated where they appear. Rotation advice past 40 comes from those two sites and from WoWSims, which is a model, and from threat and combat logs WoWSims has fitted at levels 26 to 55. No raid is open until December 9, so nothing here rests on a raid log and no source has seen a level 60 raid boss hit a bear. Bear and Cat share one talent tree and one levelling build. If a tooltip differs from the text, go by the text.

What Bear is for

Bear Form multiplies the armour on your gear by 180% and adds health that grows with level, 560 on the tooltip from level 40. Dire Bear Form at 40 makes that 360% and +1,240 health at 60. Both forms raise your threat by 115%. You can drop form to heal yourself with Mana. GrowlGrowlLevel 10 · Spell · PhysicalCastInstantRangeMeleeCooldown8 sec cooldownDuration3 secTaunts the target to attack you, but has no effect if the target is already attacking you. on an 8-second cooldown holds what you pull, and rage comes from being hit as well as from hitting. The weapon's damage counts in Bear Form, so more damage means more threat.

You do not get a choice before level 20. Bear Form comes from a class quest at 10; Cat Form does not exist until 20. Icy Veins on choosing between them later: "Often it can be faster to use Bear Form against multiple enemies, while Cat Form is better against a single enemy." Wowhead: "Can deal damage, tank, and heal between pulls with the same basic toolkit."

The class starts slowly. Wowhead: "Druids start off feeling a little slow, particularly before unlocking Bear Form at Level 10 and Cat Form at Level 20."

Expect to be asked to tank. Wowhead lists it as a cost of the spec: a Feral Druid "will frequently be expected to tank, both while leveling and in the endgame."

Your talent points

Level 60: 9/32/10, Icy Veins' levelling order (page dated November 4, built on the November 3 trees). It is one build for both forms. Spend the points in this order:

  3. Feral SwiftnessFeral SwiftnessTalent · Rank 2 of 2CastInstantIncreases your movement speed while in Cat Form by 30%, and increases your chance to Dodge by 4%. 2, levels 18 and 19

  6. Sharpened ClawsSharpened ClawsTalent · Rank 2 of 2CastInstantIncreases your critical strike chance while in Bear Form, Dire Bear Form, or Cat Form by 6%. 2, levels 23 and 24

Wowhead's tank levelling builds differ (November 6). Both are interactive calculators on its tank levelling page, and the text gives no split. The first "picks up all the relevant Feral talents first, then goes puts all its remaining points into Restoration for the later levels", to keep Mana for healing between pulls. The second goes for Nature's MajestyNature's MajestyTalent · Rank 2 of 2CastInstantIncreases your critical strike chance with spells and melee attacks by 4%. and Nature's ReachNature's ReachTalent · Rank 2 of 2CastInstantIncreases the range of your offensive Balance spells by 20% and improves your chance to hit by 4%. instead, for pulling range, and is "more mana hungry". Wowhead recommends the first "unless you have a focused and reliable leveling group."

Stat priority

For staying alive, the two sites agree on the stats and not on the order.

  1. Wowhead (November 3): Stamina, Defense to 440, armour, Agility, avoidance
  2. Icy Veins (November 4): armour, Defense to 440, Stamina, Agility, dodge

Both say so with a caveat. Icy Veins: "we do not actually know if we need 440 Defense since we have not seen Raid Bosses at Level 60 yet." 440 Defense is the figure that removes a raid boss's chance to crit you. A bear cannot block or parry, and Icy Veins adds that it cannot avoid Crushing Blows, so armour has to carry those. The armour cap against a raid boss is 17,265.

For threat: weapon DPS, then expertise and hit. Icy Veins lists weapon DPS, expertise to 6.5% and on to 14% for a tank facing a boss, hit to 8%, then Agility and Strength. WoWSims' bear weights agree on the shape: 1 weapon DPS about 3.0, a point of Stamina 0.97, Strength 0.47, Agility 0.45 (WoWSims' model).

While levelling: Stamina and armour on leather, and the highest-DPS weapon you can hold. Bear Form multiplies your gear's armour, so a leather piece with a high armour number beats the same stats on cloth.

The weapon's damage counts in Bear Form. Auto-attack DPS in form equals your weapon's DPS at a fixed 2.5-second swing, 1.0 second in Cat Form, so weapon speed does not matter.
